conventions.verified: Date a human-readable source page was fetched and the number read. All entries 2026-11-05 unless a field says otherwise.
conventions.null: null means NOT FOUND in a fetched NASA/JPL source. Never invent: see the unverified[] array of each mission.
conventions.conflicts: Where two NASA pages disagree both values are kept in notes[] and the one used in the primary field is stated.
conventions.cost: Costs are as printed by the source; year basis (real vs nominal dollars) is usually not stated by the source.
conventions.derived: Fields starting with derived_ were computed by the plan author from source numbers, with the arithmetic stated.

missions.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter

power.power_note: NSSDCA prints 'about 1850 W (end-of-life), averaging 800 W per orbit' as summarised by the fetch tool; re-read the page before relying on the EOL wording

orbit.period: initial orbit about 5 h; operational period not stated

comm.bands: S-band uplink and low-rate downlink; Ka-band high-rate downlink

missions.lifetime: 1-year exploration phase, science phase from Sept 2010, second extended science mission as of Sept 2015 (NSSDCA)
notes: NSSDCA 'Facts in Brief' lists mass 500 kg which conflicts with the 1846 kg launch mass in the body text (not used).

missions.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

power.battery: two nickel-hydrogen batteries, each 50 A-hr at 32 V (derived 1600 Wh each)

instruments.name: HiRISE
instruments.note: features ~1 m across; mass/power/data rate not on fetched pages

comm.downlink_rate_note: maximum 6 Mb/s (NSSDCA); NASA Facts: more than 10x any earlier Mars mission

missions.lifetime: planned 24-month primary science phase starting Nov 2006; operating with extensions (NSSDCA, NASA Science)
unverified: power at Mars aphelion vs perihelion

missions.name: MAVEN
missions.propellant_note: derived: 2454 - 809. Pre-launch NASA Facts gives max dry 903 kg / wet 2550 kg; the 809/2454 pair is from the NASA Science mission page (as-built).

missions.name: Juno

power.array_note: three arrays each 9 m x 2.65 m, 18,698 cells
power.power_w: ~14,000 at Earth distance; ~400 at Jupiter distance (JPL press kit). NSSDCA: 18 kW at Earth, 400 W nominal.

radiation.vault_mass_kg: 180 (NASA Science per search summary) vs 150 (NSSDCA); wall thickness up to 'over a cm' titanium
radiation.note: vault approach reused by Europa Clipper (NASA Europa Clipper press kit)

missions.instruments: 10 instruments listed by NSSDCA; mass/power not given

comm.source_note: DESCANSO Juno telecom design and performance summary

cost_musd.basis: $1.13 billion total mission investment incl. 78 months of operations (JPL press kit)

missions.lifetime: Planned end of prime mission 2018-02-20 (press kit); mission extended. NSSDCA says scheduled end Sept 2025 but the page may be stale; current 2026 status unverified.

missions.name: Europa Clipper
missions.type: flyby tour from Jupiter orbit, radiation-limited
missions.launch_mass_note: about 12,800 lb (~5,800 kg) fueled; some NASA pages round to 6,000 kg or 5,900 kg
missions.derived_dry_note: 5800 - 2750; one search summary quotes 3,241 kg (7,145 lb) from NASA but the primary page was not located: unverified

power.array_note: two arrays of five panels, each 14.2 m x 4.1 m
power.power_w: ~23,000 near launch (closer to Sun); at least 700 through prime mission

radiation.vault: aluminum-zinc alloy sheets up to 9.2 mm (0.36 in) thick
radiation.dose: electronics expect an average of a few thousand to tens of thousands of rads per flyby even with mitigation (JPL press kit)

propulsion.engines: 24 x 27.5 N, up to eight firing at once (220 N max)

missions.instruments: nine science instruments plus gravity/radio science (masses not stated)

comm.antenna: 3 m (10 ft) high-gain plus seven smaller antennas; Deep Space Network 3 stations

cost_musd.basis: approximately $5.2 billion over full mission life 2015-2034 (JPL press kit)

missions.thermal: Some components can exceed 100 C in the inner solar system; worst-case cold near -230 C at Jupiter; detectors cooled below -190 C

missions.name: Cassini-Huygens
missions.launch_mass_note: incl. fuel, Huygens probe and adapter (NASA Science quick facts; press kit says same). NSSDC catalog quotes 5,655 kg.
missions.dry_mass_note: orbiter alone 'unfueled' 2,125 kg (press kit); Huygens 320 kg; propellants about 3,132 kg (6,905 lb)

power.power_w: 885 at launch, 633 at end of mission (3 RTGs)
power.note: press kit pre-launch estimate: ~675 W at Saturn arrival

instruments.name: 12 orbiter instruments: CIRS, ISS, UVIS, VIMS, Radar, RSS, CAPS, CDA, INMS, MAG, MIMI, RPWS

comm.bands: X-band (8.4 GHz down, 7.2 GHz up), RFS output 20 W TWTA

missions.onboard_storage: two solid-state recorders, each ~2 gigabits (press kit: about 200 megabytes each), 1.8 Gbit each at end of mission
missions.downlink_volume: 635 GB science data total over the mission (NASA Science quick facts); 453,048 images

cost_musd.basis: $3.9 billion ($2.5B pre-launch + $1.4B post-launch) (NASA Science quick facts)

missions.lifetime: Primary 4 years (2004-2008), Equinox 2008-2010, Solstice 2010-2017; 13 years at Saturn
design_lessons: science instruments are body-fixed so the whole spacecraft must turn: most observations are recorded then replayed, not live
data are stored in SSRs and returned in scheduled DSN passes

missions.name: MESSENGER
missions.launch_mass_note: NSSDCA: total 1093 kg incl. 607.8 kg propellant and helium. NASA Science MESSENGER page prints 1,107.9 kg (2,443 lb). Conflict not resolved.
missions.dry_mass_note: NSSDCA Facts in Brief 'Mass: 485.2 kg' = 1093 - 607.8; not labelled dry by the page

power.power_note: nominal at Mercury orbit; arrays 70% optical solar reflectors, 30% GaAs/Ge cells
power.battery: nickel-hydrogen, 11 vessels x 2 cells; capacity not stated

orbit.note: NASA Science page prints 'approximately 5,800 x 125 miles (9,300 x 200 km), 12-hour' which does not reconcile with 15,193 km at a 12 h period; derived check: a 12 h period needs a ~10,140 km semimajor axis, i.e. apoapsis altitude ~15,200 km, matching NSSDCA
orbit.late_orbit: ~25 km minimum altitude by Sept 2014 (NASA Science)

comm.antenna: two fixed phased-array clusters plus medium and low gain

missions.lifetime: Orbit insertion 2011-03-18; primary 1 year; extended ~3 more years until propellant ran out; impact 2015-04-30
design_lessons: 12 h elliptical orbit with periapsis over the hot day side was chosen so the spacecraft spends most time far from the planet's infrared heat
sunshade-protected design; instruments on the bottom deck
unverified: the 'design lesson' about orbit geometry is the plan author's engineering inference, not a NASA quote

missions.name: Magellan

orbit.swath: each orbit ~20 km wide x 17,000 km long at 75 m/pixel

missions.coverage: 98% of surface imaged at better than 100 m resolution (design goal ~70%); 83.7% after cycle 1, 96% after cycle 2 (NASA Science)
missions.lifetime: Cycles 1-3 radar mapping (3 x 243 d), cycle 4-5 gravity, aerobraking to circular orbit 1993, ended 1994-10-12/13 plunge into atmosphere
design_lessons: mission planned as repeating 243-day cycles; each cycle is one full rotation of Venus under the orbit
left-looking then right-looking cycles trade data volume for coverage geometry
unverified: NSSDCA catalog page returned an error on 2026-11-04

missions.name: Lucy
